question.problem:
The covariance matrix $C$ of some particular observations is shown below. 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the second principal component of the data, given that the eigenvalues of $C$ are $10,$ $5,$ and $3.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the unit eigenvectors of the covariance matrix $C$ are called the principal components of the data. If 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}>{\lambda }_{2}>⋯>{\lambda }_{n}
$$

are the eigenvalues of $C$ written in descending order, then: 

- the $1$st principal component is the unit eigenvector ${u}_{1}$ corresponding to the $1$st eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1},$

- the $2$nd principal component is the unit eigenvector ${u}_{2}$ corresponding to the $2$nd eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2},$

- $⋯$

and so on.

In our case, the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix $C,$ in descending order, are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=10,\,{\lambda }_{2}=5,\,{\lambda }_{3}=3.
$$

So, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}C-5I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(C-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{2}=\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
